sections.heading: Why we are writing to you

sentences.text: We are reaching out because STX1B-related generalized epilepsy with febrile seizures plus and SLC6A1-related epilepsy with myoclonic-atonic seizures are recorded on the same mechanism road, described here as too little protein from loss of one copy.
For STX1B, the curated mechanism is loss of function, inferred, with strong confidence for the gene-disease link.
For SLC6A1, the curated mechanism is also loss of function, inferred, with definitive confidence for the gene-disease link.
The recorded phenotype similarity is high, although all of the shared weight comes from common low-information terms.
The shared features listed in the evidence pack are atonic seizure, generalized non-motor (absence) seizure, non-motor seizure, dialeptic seizure, and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder.
Registry design and natural history protocol were judged transferable between the two conditions.
Outcome measures and endpoints were also judged transferable, but age of onset and severity still need review before any instrument is adopted.
Clinical network, sites, and investigators were judged transferable, with the caution that the SLC6A1 organization listing is unverified.

sections.heading: What we would like to learn from or reuse

sentences.text: We would like to learn from any registry or natural history materials linked to SLC6A1 studies, including NCT07531511 and NCT01238250.
We would like to review outcome measures and endpoints used in those studies as possible templates for STX1B work.
We would also like to learn which clinical sites and investigators are active across the SLC6A1 natural history and interventional studies.
The evidence pack lists SLC6A1 Connect as a neighbor organization, but says the listing is unverified and that registry status is unknown.
For research planning only, we would value expert review of whether SLC6A1 therapeutic strategy, assay design, and trial design could serve as templates for STX1B.
We must not assume that a therapy approach transfers directly from SLC6A1 to STX1B.
The reason is that mechanism is recorded per gene and disease, not per family, and a family's own variant may act differently.
The evidence pack says the family's own variant class should be confirmed with a clinical geneticist before acting on any transfer idea.
We also must not assume that SLC6A1 disease models can stand in for STX1B disease models.
The reason is that the neighbor's animal or cell model is specific to its own gene, even if some assay design may be reusable after expert review.
The curated mechanism for both conditions is inferred from variant types, not from direct functional evidence.
We also must not assume eligibility for an SLC6A1 trial, because enrolment in the neighbor's trials was not asserted.
Does the overlap between STX1B and SLC6A1 go beyond common features such as seizures and developmental delay in clinical practice.
Is SLC6A1 Connect the right contact, and does it run a registry.
Has a child's specific STX1B variant been functionally classified as loss of function, gain of function, or dominant negative, and does it match the mechanism recorded for the condition.
What functional evidence exists for STX1B, given that the curated mechanism is inferred from variant types rather than functional studies.

glossary.meaning: A change that reduces how well a gene or its protein works.
The main biological way a gene change is thought to cause disease.
A study that follows people over time to learn how a condition changes.
A test, score, or observation used to track symptoms or daily function.
A doctor with special training in genetic conditions and test results.
A cell or animal system used in research to study a disease.
